title: ZeroDiff: Zero-Shot Time Series Reconstruction via Informed-Prior Diffusion
claim: A baseline built only from available inputs over-smooths extremes; our calibration step restores peaks and tracks the ground truth.
layout: 2 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, dashed box highlights the same peak region
description: Two vertically stacked line-plot panels share the same x-axis and a bold black ground-truth curve. Panel (a), titled 'Exogenous-only prior', overlays a red dashed prediction. It is smooth and offset above the truth, and it misses the sharp spikes. The red italic label 'Peaks over-smoothed' sits in the corner. Panel (b), titled 'ZeroDiff calibration', overlays a blue dashed curve. It is slightly noisy but follows the truth closely, including the tall spikes. The blue italic label 'Peaks restored' sits in the corner. A grey dashed rectangle marks the same high-peak region in both panels, so the eye goes there first. A shared legend at the bottom lists Ground truth (black solid), Exogenous prior (red dashed) and ZeroDiff (blue dashed). The whole figure is enclosed in a rounded border.
caption: In the exogenous-only reconstruction the peaks are over-smoothed and no longer stand out (a); ZeroDiff calibrates it onto the ground truth, restoring their prominence (b).
abstract: Time series modeling increasingly demands high-quality supervision, yet target observations remain scarce - exogenous inputs are broadly available, but target measurements are often unavailable due to cost, infrastructure, or accessibility constraints. Can models trained on observed locations reconstruct target time series where measurements have never been collected? We term this zero-shot time series reconstruction. A naive approach - directly mapping exogenous inputs to targets - can yield predictions at unobserved locations, but without target signals, such models fail to capture the intrinsic dynamics of the target variable, producing overly smooth outputs that underestimate extremes. This reveals systematic errors that call for explicit modeling and calibration. We propose ZeroDiff, which constructs an informed prior from exogenous variables alone, then learns to calibrate reconstruction errors through diffusion - training on observed locations and generalizing to unobserved ones. Experiments across diverse real-world datasets demonstrate significant improvements over existing approaches. Our code is available at https://github.com/YingdaFan/ZeroDiff-ICML2026.
